stages.title: Deficits and national debt
stages.sub: Why the size and persistence of national debt matters for interest costs, borrowing conditions, investors and future generations.

steps.q: A government runs a fiscal deficit every year for ten years, each one adding to what it owes. What happens to the total stock of debt over those ten years?
steps.right: It keeps growing, year after year
steps.wrong: It stays the same once the first deficit is added
steps.hint: Each year's deficit is a new flow added onto the stock already there.

steps.q: The government's debt has grown much larger. It now needs to borrow more from the same pool of savings that firms use for investment. What is likely to happen to the funds left for firms to borrow?
steps.right: Less is available for firms to borrow
steps.wrong: The same amount stays available for firms
steps.hint: Savings are limited. If government takes a bigger slice, what is left for everyone else?
